title: GlobalFoundries Breaks Ground on $10 Billion Semiconductor Fab in Malta, New York
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

GlobalFoundries (GF) broke ground on November 13, 2026, on a new $10 billion semiconductor manufacturing facility in Malta, New York, marking a significant milestone in the expansion of domestic semiconductor manufacturing.

The new 300mm wafer fabrication facility is part of a landmark U.S.-Japan investment initiative providing up to $21 billion in funding for two semiconductor fabs. Japan will provide investment capital, while GlobalFoundries will serve as the technology provider and manufacturing operator.

The first facility, supported by $570 million in New York State incentives, is expected to begin operations in 2029. When fully operational, it is projected to add approximately 900,000 300mm wafers of annual manufacturing capacity. A second planned facility would provide comparable capacity.

Together, the projects are expected to generate approximately 27,000 construction and ecosystem jobs and more than 1,000 highly skilled manufacturing positions.

Unlike leading-edge foundries focused primarily on advanced digital processors, GlobalFoundries specializes in differentiated semiconductor technologies serving automotive, industrial, communications, and connected infrastructure markets.

The expansion builds upon GF’s established manufacturing operations and semiconductor expertise in New York’s Capital Region.

Why It Matters
Although advanced AI processors dominate semiconductor headlines, foundational chips remain essential to the global economy. Automobiles, industrial equipment, communications networks, energy infrastructure, and consumer electronics depend heavily on specialty semiconductor technologies.

The Malta expansion will help diversify semiconductor supply chains and reduce dependence on overseas manufacturing.

The U.S.-Japan partnership also introduces an interesting model for semiconductor industrial policy, combining international investment with established American manufacturing expertise.

For GlobalFoundries, the investment represents an opportunity to expand manufacturing capacity while strengthening its competitive position in differentiated semiconductor technologies.

The United States needs more than leading-edge AI chip manufacturing. It also needs a resilient domestic supply of the foundational semiconductors that power the modern economy.
